newsitem.title: JAPAN: Engine trouble forces KAL jet back to airport.
newsitem.headline: Engine trouble forces KAL jet back to airport.

text.p: A Korean Air Lines (KAL) Airbus A300 en route to Seoul from Osaka returned to an airport in western Japan when it experienced engine trouble shortly after takeoff, an official of the airline said on Wednesday.

KAL flight 724, with 261 passengers and a crew of 12 on board, experienced the engine problem over the island of Awajishima, western Japan, and returned to Kansai International Airport near Osaka about 15 minutes after its 1.20 p.m. takeoff, the official said.
No one was injured in the incident and KAL was planning to reschedule the flight with a different aircraft on Wednesday evening, he said.
The airline was investigating cause of the engine problem, he added.

Earlier on Wednesday a Korean Air Lines Boeing 747 jumbo jet crashed on the U.S. Pacific island of Guam, killing more than 200 people. About 35 people survived, including some who walked away from burning wreckage.

The 747 was flying from Seoul to Guam, carrying mostly South Korean tourists and honeymooners when it crashed in heavy rain and ruptured an oil pipeline just miles from the airport. The cause of the crash is still unknown.
